346.h: Wellspring University is a private university licensed by the Federal Government in November 2009 and based on Christian principles. It was founded by the Management Science Centre, which a group of academics and professionals set up in Lagos in 1983. The centre began by coaching students of the University of Lagos correspondence institute, and by 1995 it ran certificate, diploma and degree courses in partnership with Auchi Polytechnic, the University of Ibadan and Ambrose Alli University. It went on to open Wisdom Gate High School in 2001 and Wellspring College in 2003, before founding the university. The university held its first combined convocation from 22 to 25 March 2017.
346.a: Undergraduate programmes are run in four colleges, and postgraduate programmes in a postgraduate school. All academic programmes are accredited by the National Universities Commission.
346.c: It is located in Benin City, Edo State.

223.h: Anchor University is a private Christian university owned by the Deeper Christian Life Ministry. Its approval was delayed in 2012, when Professor Celestine Onwuliri, leader of the National Universities Commission team due to make the final inspection, died with more than 150 others in the Dana Air crash in Lagos on 3 June 2012. Construction began in 2013, the Commission approved the university on 2 November 2016, and lectures began in February 2017 with 102 students in 15 courses across three faculties.
223.a: The university now has seven faculties: Humanities; Science; Social and Management Sciences; Law; Environmental Science; Basic and Allied Medical Sciences; and Education.
223.c: The campus is at Ayobo, in the Ipaja area of Lagos State.

227.h: Bauchi State University, now named Sa'adu Zungur University (SAZU), is a public university owned by the Bauchi State Government. It was part of the wave of state universities that followed the end of the federal government's monopoly on founding universities. Governor Ahmad Adamu Mu'azu set up a planning committee in 2007; his successor, Isa Yuguda, revived the effort in October 2008, and an implementation committee took the project forward from June 2009. The National Universities Commission lists 2011 as its year of establishment. The university was renamed in honour of Sa'adu Zungur, a Bauchi-born writer and pioneer of Northern Nigerian politics.
227.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes for students from Bauchi State and the wider north-east.
227.c: Its main campus is at Gadau, with further campuses at Misau and in Bauchi city.

348.h: Yobe State University (YSU) is a public university owned by the Yobe State Government. It was established under a state law in 2006 by Bukar Abba Ibrahim, executive governor of Yobe State from 1999 to 2007.
348.a: YSU has faculties of Social and Management Sciences, Agriculture, Arts and Education, Sciences and Computing, and a College of Medical and Health Sciences. Undergraduate programmes range from accountancy, business administration and economics to agriculture, biochemistry, chemistry, computer science and anatomy, and include many combined education degrees, such as education and biology or education and English, which train teachers. Postgraduate diplomas, master's degrees and doctorates are also offered, and a directorate supervises affiliated colleges.
348.c: It is located in Damaturu, the capital of Yobe State.

293.h: Landmark University is a private Christian university affiliated with the Living Faith Church Worldwide, the church that also founded Covenant University. The National Universities Commission records its establishment in 2011. Its central mission is agricultural: its leadership argues that Nigeria, once a major exporter of cash crops, became dependent on food imports after the oil boom of the 1970s, and that universities should help reverse that.
293.a: Landmark encourages students of every discipline to take up agriculture, and uses scholarships and career talks to draw Nigerian students into agriculture-related courses. It pioneered a certificate and diploma in 'agri-preneurship', on the business opportunities in farming, and it works with agricultural research and industry organisations. It also teaches engineering, the sciences and business. In 2014 it was placed among the top five universities in Nigeria by the Webometrics ranking.
293.c: The campus is at Omu-Aran in Kwara State.

229.h: Baze University is a private university in Abuja, founded by Yusuf Datti Baba-Ahmed. It received its provisional licence from the National Universities Commission on 7 March 2011 and began teaching that year with 17 students, all in one building on its 50,000-square-metre site. Buildings for administration and for the faculties of law, computing and applied sciences, engineering, environmental sciences, and medical and health sciences followed, and work on a university teaching hospital began in 2021.
229.a: Baze runs 43 undergraduate degree programmes as well as postgraduate degrees, across faculties that include Management and Social Sciences, Law, Computing and Applied Sciences, Engineering, Environmental Sciences, and Medical and Health Sciences. It has held six consecutive convocations.
229.c: The campus in Abuja has a library, staff housing and two student hostels, one for men and one for women, each holding about 500 students.

308.h: Oduduwa University is a private university established in 2009 and named after Oduduwa, regarded as the ancestor of the Yoruba people. It is accredited by the National Universities Commission.
308.a: The university has four colleges. Management and Social Sciences offers business administration, mass communication, economics, banking and finance, accounting, public administration, political science and international relations. Natural and Applied Sciences covers mathematics and statistics, computer science, physics with electronics, chemistry and biochemistry, and microbiology. Environmental Design and Management teaches architecture, estate management and quantity surveying, and Engineering and Technology offers computer, electrical and electronic, and mechanical engineering. Centres for ICT and for entrepreneurial and vocational training support the colleges.
308.c: It is located in Ipetumodu, near Ile-Ife, in Osun State.
